title: PEF-Adjuvant – Shared Decision-Making for Adjuvant Systemic Therapy in Melanoma: A Multicentre, Prospective, Cluster-Randomised Implementation Study Using a Stepped-Wedge Design
summary:
The number of cases of black skin cancer (melanoma) is steadily increasing and accounts for more than 90 percent of all skin cancer deaths in Germany. People with melanoma in an intermediate stage (stage IIB/C or III) face an important decision after surgery: whether or not to start an additional (“adjuvant”) drug treatment. This can be a difficult choice – the treatment can lower the risk of the cancer coming back, but it can also cause serious side effects. Many patients feel uncertain or not well supported when making this decision.
The project “PEF-Adjuvant” aims to change that. Its goal is to help patients take an active and informed role in deciding about their treatment — a process called “shared decision-making” (PEF).
The project includes three parts:
• a structured PEF training for doctors,
• an activation flyer for patients, and
• a digital decision aid with videos, graphics, and interactive content tailored to each patient’s cancer stage and mutation status.
The study takes place at six leading skin cancer centers in Germany. It examines how these measures affect medical outcomes, quality of life, and psychological aspects such as uncertainty, regret, and participation. In addition, interviews with patients and doctors will help to better understand their experiences and views.
The project fills an important gap in care, as no such german decision aid currently exists for this patient group. By improving communication and supporting informed decisions, PEF-Adjuvant aims to reduce over- and under-treatment and, in the long term, improve patient satisfaction, adherence to therapy, and the efficient use of healthcare resources.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with melanoma in stages IIB/C or III, after surgical removal of the primary tumor and any affected lymph nodes, who are eligible for adjuvant systemic therapy.
Exclusion criteria:
Not legally competent; patients who, due to physical or mental impairments or insufficient German language skills, are unable to use the PtDA and/or complete the questionnaires.
